clue.text: Sound of disapproval as mostly tough beefsteak presented to husband

indicators.note: presented to means the first pieces come before the next one
mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: tough means hard
rump steak is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles as their husband is served a chewy beefsteak.
explanation.walkthrough: Rump is a cut of beef sold as steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrumph is the gruff throat-clearing noise people make to signal displeasure.

clue.text: Overacting allowed in play

parts.note: ham acting is exaggerated performing
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Hammy performance is permitted on stage in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Hamlet lectures the players against overacting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince.

clue.text: Discount senior journalist entering row

indicators.note: entering means the journalist goes into the row

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy quarrel
ED, the editor

explanation.surface: The editor walks into a newsroom argument over price cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a cut in price, the same as a discount.

clue.text: Leaving appeal, dim European remains free

indicators.note: leaving means the appeal letters go out of the word

parts.note: unlit means dark, dim
IT is sex appeal
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A dull European departs, abandoning charm, and stays free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to release or set loose, like a dog off its lead.

clue.text: Writings from scribes or poets turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down answer means reading upwards, so backwards
from means the letters are taken out of the run of clue words

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of scribes, or and the start of poets holds the word backwards

explanation.surface: Pieces of text appear from scribes or poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose is ordinary written language, the stuff of writings not in verse.

clue.text: Switzerland backs place beginning to suppress coup

indicators.note: backs means Switzerland's letters come at the back of the answer

parts.note: to place is to put

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of suppress
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Swiss forces back a site from which to crush an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden violent attempt to seize government, a German word for an overthrow.

clue.text: Make economies to no avail

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split as USE LESS the answer means to economise; whole it means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless describes an effort that achieved nothing, the same as one made in vain.

clue.text: Sensational wine Tesco essentially is introducing

indicators.note: introducing means the central letter comes in front of the wine
essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

parts.note: middle letter of Tesco
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: A supermarket chain's wine is said to be a sensational offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock result is a startling, sensational one; shock works as an adjective here.

clue.text: Self-indulgent type, that man isn't mobile after party

parts.note: he refers to that man
a do is a party

indicators.note: mobile means the letters move about

explanation.surface: After a party, a man is too sluggish to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist pursues pleasure for its own sake, a self-indulgent person.

clue.text: Old actors taking up golf displaying giddiness

indicators.note: taking up means the actors absorb the golf letter

parts.note: old stagers are veteran actors
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Veteran thespians who take up golf turn dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who staggers is reeling unsteadily, which shows dizziness.

clue.text: Type of music from odd Adele hit, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A critic notes a strange chart success by the singer Adele and asks what genre it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road music is bland, mainstream easy listening that avoids extremes.

clue.text: Surround Conservative student in eastern church's central area

indicators.note: in means the Conservative and student letters go inside the church's central area

parts.note: the nave is the main central part of a church
L is the learner plate letter, a student driver

explanation.surface: A Tory and a student stand in the middle of an Orthodox church.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, enclave means to enclose or surround, though the noun is far more familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The rarer verb sense of enclave is to enclose a place within foreign territory, i.e. to hem it in.

clue.text: Towering figure in London that's usually pickled?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 30 St Mary Axe, the City of London skyscraper nicknamed the ...
second meaning: a small cucumber normally eaten preserved in vinegar

explanation.walkthrough: The Gherkin is a bullet-shaped London office tower named for its resemblance to the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The building's nickname comes from the small cucumber that is preserved in vinegar.

clue.text: How Ibsen upset part of Turkey, maybe

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks how the playwright Ibsen offended part of the nation of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T disguises the bird as the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The wishbone is the forked breastbone of a bird such as a turkey, pulled apart for luck.

clue.text: Switch positions occasionally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two settings of a switch
second meaning: intermittently, now and then

explanation.definitionFit: On and off names a switch's two states and also means intermittently, from time to time.

clue.text: Fish son succeeded to trap surfaces

indicators.note: to trap means the two outer letters hold the fish between them

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A son manages to catch a fish as it rises to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The sides of an object are its faces or outer planes.

clue.text: Hysterical and exasperated over debts

indicators.note: over in a down answer means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: riled means irritated, exasperated
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: Someone goes frantic and furious about money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirious means wildly excited or frenzied, beside oneself.

clue.text: Outside volunteers around supply bananas for mammal

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters sit outside the volunteers
bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
around means the volunteers are turned round

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers go crazy delivering supplies to an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal with a duck-like bill.

clue.text: Pleasure boat denied American afternoon meal

indicators.note: denied means the American letter is refused a place in the word

parts.note: a launch is a motorboat used for pleasure trips

explanation.surface: An American is turned away from a pleasure cruise and misses the afternoon meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the meal eaten around midday or in the early afternoon.

clue.text: Recently stolen car producing tricky situation

parts.note: hot goods are freshly stolen
SEAT is a Spanish car maker

explanation.surface: A newly stolen vehicle lands someone in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat means facing pressure or awkward questioning.

clue.text: Construction company

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the putting together of parts
second meaning: a gathering of people

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a building firm; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembly covers both fitting components together and a body of people gathered in one place.

clue.text: Love for university in German city is enormous

indicators.note: for means the love letter takes the place of the university letter

parts.note: Münster is a city in north-west Germany
love is nil in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Romance replaces studies in a German city on a huge scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Monster as an adjective means huge, as in a monster sale.

clue.text: Bulgarian ready to acquire English ship, revolutionary craft

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning right round, so reading backwards
to acquire means the Bulgarian money takes in the other letters

parts.note: the lev is Bulgaria's currency; ready is cash
SS, steamship

explanation.surface: Bulgarian cash buys an English ship, a radical vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready (or readies) is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a ship or boat, any craft for water.

clue.text: Browned off at toes getting cold ultimately

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoiled and come out jumbled
ultimately points to the very last letter

parts.note: last letter of cold

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up because their toes are getting chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is British slang for fed up, but here it splits into definition and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasted bread has been browned by heat under a grill.

clue.text: In the middle of morning good number will regress

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem

indicators.note: will regress means going backwards, so read in reverse

explanation.surface: At midmorning, a good number of things will slip back.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means surrounded by, in the midst of a group.

clue.text: Disquiet fell-runner ventures to admit

indicators.note: to admit means the clue words take the answer in, holding it inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of fell-runner and the start of ventures spell the word

explanation.surface: A mountain runner owns up to feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell-runner races over hills, fells being upland moors in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To disquiet someone is to make them anxious, to rattle their nerve.

clue.text: Treatment of you and me in prison, stripped

parts.note: us means you and me

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are removed

parts.note: caged means locked up

explanation.surface: How we are handled when locked up and searched.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something or someone is handled, as in rough usage.

clue.text: Peculiar groups seen circling King's quarters possibly

parts.note: proper in the sense of peculiar to, belonging specifically

indicators.note: circling means the groups go round the king's letter

parts.note: factions are groups within a larger body
R for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Odd cliques gather around the monarch's living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' means particular here (proper to), not strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one example of a fraction smaller than one, which mathematicians call proper.

clue.text: Reportedly names places of interest

indicators.note: reportedly means we go by how the word is heard when spoken

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A guidebook supposedly lists the tourist attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: The sights of a town are its attractions worth seeing on a tour.

clue.text: Both sides receiving praise for resolving compensation

indicators.note: receiving means the side letters take the rearranged word between them

parts.note: right and left, R and L

indicators.note: resolving means working the word into a new form

explanation.surface: Two parties welcome compliments as a way of settling a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: An old sense of reprisal is the seizure of goods in compensation for a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a reprisal was redress or indemnity taken from an enemy for damage suffered.
